findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Inspectors observed a build up of ice in the walk-in cooler at the bottom of the door of the walk-in freezer. A build up of ice was also observed behind the refrigeration unit in the walk-in freezer. PIC was made aware. PIC ensured inspectors that the building up will be cleaned. Ensure that the build up is clean to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

 Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  
Observed employee put on gloves and begin to work with food without washing hands. Tartar sauce was being dipped from a bulk container into a squeeze bottle. The proper use of single use gloves and hand washing was discussed thoroughly.

findings.title: Food received at proper temperature
findings.comment:
3-202.11: (A) TCS FOOD shall be at 41F or below when received-P. (B) If specified by LAW, FOOD may be received at different temperature-P. (C) Eggs shall be received at 45F-P. (D) TCS FOODS already cooked shall be received at 135F or above-P. (E) Frozen FOOD shall be received frozen (Pf). (F) TCS FOOD shall be free of evidence of temperature abuse -Pf.
Food was received at 125F. It was placed into the oven for hot holding. By the time it was served the internal temperature had reached 133F. The facility is going to move to time as a control for delivery and service of food for the children. Employee arrives at cooking facility around 10am and takes food as soon as it is prepared to the school. The first round of food is finished cooking between 10:15 and 10:30 and is served by 11am. Time and temperature will be placed on the food transfer bags and food shall be served or discarded within 4 hours. At time of inspection, the items served are all pre cooked, frozen proteins.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Observed spray nozzle of dish machine area to have accumulation of grime and debris on top of and under nozzle (as well as the squeezer). Ensure routine cleaning of NonFOOD-contact surfaces in order to hinder debris build-up.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

Observed no test strips for both bleach and quaternary ammonium. Provided educational regarding both types of test strips, appropriate concentration levels, and overuse of bleach. Inspector will follow-up on 12/28/20.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

Observed caulk to be coming away from dish machine area. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11  (Pf) Working container of sanitizer not properly labeled. Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

Observed multiple sanitizer spray bottles to lack a label. Discussed reasoning for common name labels on spray bottles with PIC. PIC labeled all spray bottles. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

Observed facility to lack test strips and/or a maximum registering thermometer in order to test heat level of dish machine. Discussed purchasing test strips and/or thermometer with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 2/27/20.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: The sanitizer level in the 3 part sink was 10 or less parts per million. The water in the third part was 126F. 750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Do not use water that is too hot as it will drive the chlorine out of solution. Also test water in sink to make sure that the sanitizer concentration is 50ppm for one minute of contact time.
